cell_type_model: mouse extra-embryonic endoderm stem-cell and embryonic Nodal/Cripto receptor systems; human comparator literature
assay_or_perturbation: Nodal or Cripto perturbation with ACVR2B/ACVR1B receptor-complex assays and p-SMAD2/3 or reporter readouts
relation_type: TDGF1/Cripto is a Nodal co-receptor in an ACVR2B-containing complex; the submitted TDGF1-ACVR2B binary edge is not isolated
pathway_branch: Nodal + TDGF1/Cripto + ACVR2B/ACVR1B -> SMAD2/3 -> Nodal transcriptional response
limitations: Primary studies support Cripto recruitment of Nodal to ACVR2B/ACVR1B complexes, while Cripto contacts Nodal and type-I receptor components rather than establishing TDGF1 as a direct ACVR2B ligand. Receptor stoichiometry and exact binary binding remain unresolved; no SCI receiver model or terminal TF assignment.

cell_type_model: mouse mammary epithelial EpH4 cells; COS7 transfectants; recombinant or overexpressed human Cripto-1/Glypican-1 contexts
assay_or_perturbation: Cripto-1 expression or soluble protein, Glypican-1 co-immunoprecipitation, GPC1 siRNA, and phospho-Src/MAPK/Akt assays
relation_type: Cripto-1 directly binds Glypican-1 and activates a Nodal/ALK4-independent Src-dependent relay
pathway_branch: TDGF1/Cripto-1 -> GPC1 -> c-Src -> MAPK and PI3K-AKT -> proliferation/migration/survival
limitations: The receptor-like partner is a GPI-anchored heparan-sulfate proteoglycan rather than a classical signaling receptor; studies use overexpression or recombinant/soluble Cripto and tumor-associated mammary models, not SCI receiver cells. No terminal TF was assigned.

cell_type_model: human gastric mucosa and isolated gastric mucin preparations
assay_or_perturbation: Gel filtration, immunoprecipitation, Western transfer, calcium/EDTA perturbation, and mucin localization
relation_type: TFF1 dimer associates directly with MUC5AC mucin in the gastric mucus layer
pathway_branch: TFF1 -> MUC5AC mucin packaging/barrier organization; no intracellular receptor relay demonstrated
limitations: The evidence is extracellular mucin binding and co-packaging, not activation of an intracellular receptor or pathway. Glycosylation, calcium, and gastric tissue context affect the interaction; no SCI receiver model or terminal TF was assigned.

cell_type_model: Jurkat lymphoblasts; CXCR4-negative/positive AGS gastric cells; KATO III and AsPC-1 cancer cells
assay_or_perturbation: Recombinant mouse or human TFF2 stimulation, CXCR4 expression, SDF-1 desensitization, AMD3100 or anti-CXCR4 blockade, calcium, MAPK, chemotaxis, and proliferation assays
relation_type: CXCR4-dependent TFF2 receptor activation with downstream MAPK and cellular responses; no purified TFF2-CXCR4 affinity assay
pathway_branch: TFF2 -> CXCR4 -> Ca2+ and MAPK signaling -> altered SDF-1 chemotaxis/proliferation
limitations: The primary study establishes receptor dependence through pharmacology and receptor gain-of-function rather than direct biochemical binding. TFF2 concentrations were high and models were lymphoid or gastrointestinal cancer cells; no SCI receiver model or terminal TF was assigned.

cell_type_model: human gastric mucus and mucin glycopeptide/overlay assays; porcine gastric mucin comparator
assay_or_perturbation: TFF2 lectin binding to alpha-GlcNAc-capped MUC6 glycans, glycan competition, overlay/size-exclusion assays, and TFF2 depletion/reconstitution
relation_type: TFF2 directly recognizes MUC6-associated glycans and contributes to mucus-barrier organization
pathway_branch: TFF2 -> MUC6 glycan binding -> gastric mucus barrier stabilization and Helicobacter pylori-restrictive context
limitations: This is a glycan/mucin interaction rather than a transmembrane receptor relay; the core protein and glycoform requirements are context-dependent. No intracellular signaling edge or terminal TF was inferred.

cell_type_model: No exact TFF3-ACKR3 cellular model located; TFF3 receptor pharmacology and ACKR3 ligand/effector comparator systems
assay_or_perturbation: Bounded exact-pair PubMed and publisher search; comparator TFF3 testing at CXCR4 did not establish ACKR3 activation
relation_type: No qualifying exact TFF3 -> ACKR3 interaction or relay located
pathway_branch: TFF3 -> ACKR3 exact edge; ACKR3 ligand/effector comparator context only
limitations: ACKR3 is an atypical scavenging/beta-arrestin receptor and TFF3 receptor claims remain unresolved. CXCL12/ACKR3 and TFF3/CXCR4 comparator findings were not transferred to this exact pair; no terminal TF was assigned.

species: human; recombinant protein and cancer-cell comparator systems
cell_type_model: COS-7 cells overexpressing CXCR4; colon carcinoma cells and TFF3-associated functional models
assay_or_perturbation: TFF3 or TFF3 homodimer IP1 assay with CXCR4, CXCR4-related functional/cancer assays, and TFF3 loss/gain perturbation
relation_type: TFF3-CXCR4 receptor assignment is unresolved: direct pharmacology was negative in a CXCR4 assay, while other studies report CXCR4-associated functional hypotheses
pathway_branch: Proposed TFF3 -> CXCR4 -> PLC/PKC or survival signaling remains unconfirmed; observed TFF3 anti-apoptotic outputs are not a direct relay
limitations: A primary pharmacology study found neither TFF3 monomeric probe nor homodimer activated CXCR4 up to 10 micromolar, and did not antagonize CXCL12. Other functional studies treat CXCR4 as a hypothesis or association; no direct binding, reproducible receptor activation, SCI model, or terminal TF assignment.

cell_type_model: Human monocytes with tissue-factor expression
assay_or_perturbation: FVIIa and TFPI stimulation, TFPI C-terminal-domain requirement, LRP blockade with receptor-associated protein, clathrin/adaptin colocalization, and TF half-life assays
relation_type: TFPI forms an inhibitory TF-FVIIa complex that couples F3 downregulation to LRP-dependent internalization
pathway_branch: TFPI + FVIIa-F3 complex -> LRP-dependent endocytosis/degradation -> reduced surface TF/F3
limitations: The exact molecular unit is a TF-FVIIa-TFPI ternary inhibitory complex and the internalizing receptor is LRP1; TFPI is not an agonist of isolated F3. The assay is a monocyte coagulation context, not SCI, and no terminal TF was assigned.

cell_type_model: Human monocytes; mouse vascular/endothelial and fibroblast receptor-clearance comparator systems
assay_or_perturbation: TFPI C-terminal receptor-binding/internalization assays, receptor-associated-protein blockade, TF downregulation, and TFPI-overexpression/clearance studies
relation_type: TFPI C-terminal region engages LRP1-family endocytic machinery in a ligand-dependent receptor-proximal clearance relay
pathway_branch: TFPI -> LRP1 -> clathrin-mediated internalization/clearance; in the TF/FVIIa context, reduced TF surface abundance
limitations: LRP1 involvement is strongest in the TF-FVIIa-TFPI bridging context; TFPI also binds heparan sulfate and other lipoprotein-receptor family members. Exact domain affinity and SCI-cell transfer remain unresolved; no terminal TF was assigned.

cell_type_model: No exact TFPI-SDC4 loss/gain or reconstitution model located; heparan-sulfate proteoglycan comparator systems
assay_or_perturbation: Exact-pair search across PubMed, PMC, and primary TFPI clearance studies; TFPI binding to heparan sulfate was not resolved to syndecan-4
relation_type: No qualifying exact TFPI -> SDC4 interaction or relay located
pathway_branch: TFPI -> SDC4 exact edge; heparan-sulfate and LRP/VLDLR comparator context only
limitations: TFPI-heparan-sulfate and TFPI-LRP/VLDLR findings do not identify SDC4 as the receptor. Related proteoglycan biology was retained only as a search boundary; no terminal TF was assigned.

cell_type_model: Mouse embryonic fibroblasts and vascular-directed TFPI-overexpression/clearance models
assay_or_perturbation: TFPI C-terminal fragment, VLDL uptake, VLDLR knockdown, and heparinase perturbation
relation_type: TFPI-associated VLDL/VLDLR uptake and clearance function; a clean binary TFPI-VLDLR affinity measurement was not established
pathway_branch: TFPI C-terminal context -> VLDLR/HSPG-assisted VLDL binding and internalization -> altered lipoprotein handling
limitations: The primary work shows VLDLR dependence in a TFPI-fragment/VLDL uptake context, but much of the uptake is attributed to heparan-sulfate proteoglycans and coordinated VLDL receptors. It does not establish a standalone TFPI-VLDLR signaling relay or terminal TF.

cell_type_model: Human or rat thyroid follicular cell models and apical thyroglobulin uptake/suppression assays
assay_or_perturbation: Thyroglobulin phosphorylation, ASGPR blockade/competition, thyroid-restricted gene expression, and TG uptake/function readouts
relation_type: ASGR1-associated thyroglobulin binding/internalization produces receptor-dependent suppressive thyroid-cell signaling
pathway_branch: TG -> ASGR1 -> altered TTF1/TTF2/PAX8, NIS, TPO, TG, and TSHR transcriptional program
limitations: The study uses an apical asialoglycoprotein receptor complex and phosphorylated TG, with species and receptor-composition caveats. It does not define a cytoplasmic ASGR1 adaptor relay or an SCI receiver context; no terminal TF was assigned.

cell_type_model: Mouse thyroid follicular cells, primary cilia, and thyroid-specific cilia-deficient mice
assay_or_perturbation: TSH stimulation, Lrp2/megalin localization, Tg uptake/endocytosis, cilia loss, and thyroid hormone/Tg phenotypes
relation_type: LRP2/megalin-mediated thyroglobulin endocytosis and thyroid follicular function
pathway_branch: TSH -> primary cilia/LRP2 -> TG endocytosis and thyroid follicular hormone-handling output
limitations: The evidence is receptor-mediated uptake and tissue function rather than a defined intracellular relay from LRP2. Multiple apical TG uptake receptors may contribute, and the model is thyroid-specific mouse tissue, not SCI; no terminal TF was assigned.

cell_type_model: No exact TG-TPO binding or receptor-dependent cellular model located; TSH-stimulated thyroid transcription comparator
assay_or_perturbation: Exact-pair search; TSH regulates TG and TPO expression, but TPO is an enzyme/output component rather than an established TG receptor
relation_type: No qualifying exact TG -> TPO interaction or relay located
pathway_branch: TG -> TPO exact edge; TSH/TSHR-regulated TG and TPO transcription is comparator function only
limitations: TSH/TSHR control of TG and TPO transcription and TG uptake by ASGR1/LRP2 do not establish TG as a TPO ligand. No direct interaction or intracellular relay was inferred; no terminal TF was assigned.

cell_type_model: Mouse lung adenocarcinoma cells; heterologous ErbB receptor transfectants
assay_or_perturbation: TGF-alpha stimulation with ErbB3 immunoprecipitation, PI3K/p85 and phosphotyrosine readouts, EGFR inhibition, and ErbB ligand-specificity comparisons
relation_type: TGF-alpha can drive EGFR-dependent ErbB3 complex signaling in cells, but direct TGFA-ErbB3 binding/activation is not established
pathway_branch: TGFA -> EGFR/ERBB2 -> ERBB3-p85 -> PI3K-AKT context; exact direct TGFA-ERBB3 edge unresolved
limitations: The primary cellular study shows TGF-alpha-induced ErbB3 association and signaling that is blocked by EGFR inhibition; it does not isolate ErbB3 as the ligand-binding receptor. TGF-alpha specificity is strongest for EGFR, and no SCI receiver model or terminal TF was assigned.

cell_type_model: IL-3-dependent murine 32D cells expressing ErbB4 with receptor-specific comparator transfectants
assay_or_perturbation: TGF-alpha stimulation, ErbB4 expression, receptor tyrosine phosphorylation, substrate phosphorylation, and ErbB2/ErbB4 co-expression comparisons
relation_type: TGF-alpha functions as an ErbB4-activating ligand in a defined heterologous receptor system
pathway_branch: TGFA -> ERBB4 (with ERBB2 co-receptor context) -> receptor/substrate phosphorylation and mitogenic signaling
limitations: The primary result is a heterologous overexpression system and does not establish the dominant physiological receptor usage in SCI. ErbB4 isoform and dimer context affect response; no terminal TF was assigned.

cell_type_model: human epithelial EMT models, mouse/NIH-3T3 receptor systems, and in-vitro kinase assays
assay_or_perturbation: TGF-beta stimulation, receptor kinase inhibitors, ACVR1/TGFBR1 perturbation, in-vitro kinase reactions, p-SMAD1/5 and EMT readouts
relation_type: TGF-beta receptor-complex cross-talk activates ACVR1 through TGFBR1/TGFBR2-associated signaling; receptor-complex composition remains context-dependent
pathway_branch: TGFB1 -> TGFBR2/TGFBR1-associated complex -> ACVR1 -> SMAD1/5 and EMT; canonical SMAD2/3 branch remains parallel
limitations: The primary work supports TGF-beta-induced ACVR1 activation and TGFBR1-mediated ACVR1 phosphorylation, but does not prove that all three submitted receptor components form one stable ligand-bound tetramer in every model. No terminal TF was assigned.

cell_type_model: FOP mouse embryonic fibroblasts and receptor-mutant/defined TGF-beta receptor systems
assay_or_perturbation: TGF-beta stimulation of ACVR1-R206H, receptor clustering/autophosphorylation, TGFBR2 dependence, and SMAD1/5 readouts
relation_type: TGF-beta can engage a TGFBR2-associated ACVR1 mutant relay, but wild-type exact ACVR1-TGFBR2 signaling without TGFBR1 is not established
pathway_branch: TGFB1 -> TGFBR2-associated ACVR1(R206H) -> SMAD1/5 in FOP context; wild-type branch unresolved
limitations: The strongest primary evidence is a gain-of-function ACVR1-R206H/FOP model, where TGFBR2 is implicated as the relevant type-II receptor. It cannot be generalized to a normal TGFB1-ACVR1-TGFBR2 complex or SCI receiver cells; no terminal TF was assigned.

cell_type_model: Caveolae and TGF-beta receptor-expressing cultured cells
assay_or_perturbation: Caveolin-1 co-immunoprecipitation with TGFBR1, caveolin scaffolding-domain perturbation, TGF-beta stimulation, and p-SMAD2/downstream response assays
relation_type: CAV1 binds and dampens the TGFBR1 receptor pathway; the submitted ligand-CAV1 pair is pathway modulation, not direct TGFB1 binding
pathway_branch: TGFB1 -> TGFBR1/TGFBR2 -> SMAD2; CAV1 scaffolding interaction suppresses receptor-proximal signaling
limitations: The primary study demonstrates CAV1-TGFBR1 interaction and inhibition of TGF-beta-induced SMAD2 phosphorylation, not a direct TGFB1-CAV1 molecular edge. Caveolar localization and cell context are essential; no terminal TF was assigned.

cell_type_model: Primary human monocyte-derived macrophages, rat microglia, and choroid-retinal endothelial cells
assay_or_perturbation: TGF-beta1 treatment, CXCR4/CXCR7 expression measurements, CXCL12-induced ERK or migration/tube-formation assays, and TGFBR inhibition
relation_type: TGF-beta1 increases CXCR4 expression and subsequent CXCL12-CXCR4 responsiveness; no direct TGFB1-CXCR4 receptor interaction
pathway_branch: TGFB1 -> TGFBR/SMAD or non-SMAD regulation -> CXCR4 expression -> CXCL12-induced ERK/migration
limitations: The evidence is pathway cross-talk and receptor-expression priming, not TGFB1 binding to CXCR4. Effects vary by macrophage, microglial, endothelial, and tumor context; no SCI receiver model or terminal TF was assigned.

cell_type_model: Human dermal fibroblasts, fibroblasts, and profibrotic TGF-beta cell models
assay_or_perturbation: TGF-beta1 pretreatment, EGF-dependent growth/EGFR binding, ERBB ligand expression, receptor phosphorylation, and pathway-inhibitor perturbations
relation_type: TGF-beta1 primes or transactivates EGFR/ERBB signaling through cross-talk; it is not a direct TGFB1-EGFR ligand-receptor assignment
pathway_branch: TGFB1 -> TGFBR/SMAD and ERBB-ligand induction -> EGFR/ERBB signaling -> growth or profibrotic outputs
limitations: Primary studies support TGF-beta/EGFR cross-talk and altered EGF responsiveness, but not direct binding of TGF-beta1 to EGFR. Cell type and induced-ligand context are decisive; no terminal TF was assigned.

cell_type_model: human umbilical-vein endothelial cells and U-937 monocytic cells; endoglin transfectants
assay_or_perturbation: 125I-TGF-beta1 affinity labeling, endoglin immunoprecipitation, endoglin isoform transfection, TGF-beta1 stimulation, proliferation, c-myc, adhesion, PECAM-1, and aggregation assays
relation_type: Endoglin directly binds TGF-beta1 and modulates receptor-complex signaling and TGF-beta-dependent cellular responses
pathway_branch: TGFB1 -> ENG/TGFBR complex -> context-dependent SMAD and endothelial/monocyte functional outputs
limitations: Endoglin is a type-III TGF-beta co-receptor/modulator, not an autonomous kinase receptor, and isoform/cell context changes the response. The evidence is vascular/monocytic rather than SCI-specific; no terminal TF was assigned.

cell_type_model: Human/mouse epithelial and pulmonary cell systems; latent TGF-beta1/LAP and alpha-v-beta6 receptor models
assay_or_perturbation: Alpha-v-beta6 binding to latent TGF-beta1 LAP, integrin expression/activation perturbation, cell-based TGF-beta activation, and in-vivo pulmonary inflammation/fibrosis assays
relation_type: Integrin alpha-v-beta6 directly binds latent TGF-beta1 LAP and mechanically activates the latent cytokine
pathway_branch: Latent TGFB1-LAP -> ITGAV_ITGB6 -> local TGF-beta1 activation -> TGFBR/SMAD and inflammatory/fibrotic outputs
limitations: The integrin recognizes the LAP/prodomain of latent TGF-beta1, not necessarily mature free TGFB1, and activation requires matrix, force, and cell context. The model is pulmonary/epithelial rather than SCI receiver tissue; no terminal TF was assigned.

cell_type_model: Human WI-38 lung fibroblasts, mouse fibroblasts, and integrin/TGF-beta matrix comparator systems
assay_or_perturbation: TGF-beta1 stimulation, integrin beta-1 mRNA/protein and surface-expression assays, Smad/EMT perturbation, and latent-TGF-beta LAP-integrin binding comparisons
relation_type: TGF-beta1 regulates beta-1 integrin expression and latent-TGF-beta may bind alpha-v-beta1 complexes; isolated ITGB1 is not a complete receptor assignment
pathway_branch: TGFB1 -> TGFBR/SMAD -> ITGB1/alpha-beta1 expression and matrix-adhesion remodeling
limitations: The strongest direct binding evidence is for an alpha-v-beta1 heterodimer or latent-LAP context, while the submitted beta-1 subunit alone is not a ligand-binding receptor. TGF-beta-induced integrin expression is downstream function, not direct TGFB1-ITGB1 binding; no terminal TF was assigned.

cell_type_model: Recombinant latent TGF-beta1/3 LAP and alpha-v-beta3 receptor assays; human WI-38 fibroblasts and mouse fibroblast comparators
assay_or_perturbation: LAP-integrin binding and receptor assays, TGF-beta1-induced integrin expression, and alpha-v-beta3 activation/function comparisons
relation_type: Latent TGFB1-LAP engages the alpha-v-beta3 heterodimer, but the exact ITGB3-only submitted edge is unresolved
pathway_branch: Latent TGFB1-LAP -> ITGAV_ITGB3 -> integrin/TGF-beta activation context; direct isolated ITGB3 relay not established
limitations: The primary binding study tests alpha-v-beta3, not beta3 alone, and lower-affinity alpha-v integrins do not uniformly activate latent TGF-beta. TGF-beta-induced beta3 expression is a separate downstream effect; no SCI receiver model or terminal TF was assigned.
